newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA STILL SEES FINNISH 1997 GDP GROWTH AT 4 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ETLA STILL SEES FINNISH 1997 GDP GROWTH AT 4 PCT.

text.p: The Finnish economy is still on
track for GDP growth of four percent this year and 3.5 percent
next year, a domestic economic think-tank said on Wednesday,
keeping its March growth forecasts unchanged.
"The volume indices for industrial output and GDP indicate
swift year-on-year growth," the Research Institute of the
Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a summary of its 1997/2 forecast.
"Inflation for this year as a whole is predicted to be one
percent." ETLA said, also repeating its March forecast. "Next
year consumer prices will rise by 1.7 percent."
ETLA also left its forecast for the 1997 unemployment rate
unchanged at 14.6 percent and for 1998 also unrevised at 13.6
In 1997-2001, Finland's GDP would grow by an average 3.5
percent per year, ETLA said, adding that rate would be one
percentage point higher than in European Union countries on
"It is anticipated that monetary policy will begin to be
tightened next year, but it will still be relatively lax," ETLA
said, adding: "The future stringency of monetary policy will
hinge upon inflationary pressures in the EU countries."
